If we use the Biden era SCC, this rule would impose another $1.47 trillion (3% discount rate), which dwarfs the purported benefits of the rule.

Using the much smaller Trump SCCs, we would see additional costs ranging from $13.5-267.8 billion through 2055.

Next, I used a range of social costs of carbon (SCCs), including the Biden era SCC ($208 in 2024$) and low, medium, and high SCCs from Trump’s first term $1.5, $9, and $13 per ton, respectively). I got these from FHWA’s modeling for its proposed fuel economy rule.

To quantify the costs of the criteria pollutants, I used EPA’s COBRA model. EPA leadership apparently no longer trusts this model, but it’s still posted on their website, and EPA staff have advised me to use it for projects on several occasions, so we’re using it.
www.epa.gov/cobra

From 2027-2055, EPA estimates that repealing the Endangerment Finding and GHG standard for vehicles will:
•	Increase GHGs by 8,212 MMTCO2e
•	Increase NOx by  1,733,847 tons
•	Increase PM2.5 by  29,840 tons
•	Reduce SO2 by  179,947 tons
•	Increase VOCs by  2,487,057 tons

In this memo, EPA lays out estimated changes in GHGs and criteria pollutants (NOx, PM2.5, SO2, and VOCs) from light- and medium-duty and heavy-duty vehicles. I spent a few days analyzing the impacts of these increased emissions of GHGs and criteria pollutants.

If you go into the Endangerment Finding docket, you can find a memo titled "Projected Criteria, Air Toxics, and GHG Emissions Impacts for the Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding and Motor Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards Under the Clean Air Act Final Rule"

Normally EPA would document how a rule affects criteria pollutant and GHG emissions in the rule itself. At the very least it would document this in the Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA). But, despite its pledge to quantify the emissions, you won’t find any estimates in the rule or RIA.

🧵 In its Endangerment Finding rescission, US EPA chose to ignore the effects of the rule on public health and the environment by refusing to even quantify them or report them in the rule.

So I dug into the docket to quantify those costs myself, using EPA's own models.
